lines.text: Every new agent starts blank, and asks the same questions. Where are the tests? How do we deploy?
So you answer every time. You paste the same paragraph into every chat, and hope you did not leave a step out.
Workspace memory fixes that. The first agent writes the answers down once, in the workspace.
So the first agent that works it out saves a short entry, with a name like how to run tests.
Then deploy steps, the port quirk, and the code style. Each gets its own entry, linked from one index.
Now a new agent loads the index before it starts. It reads the titles, and opens what it needs.
So it does not ask. It runs the tests the right way, the first time.
It does not matter which agent shows up, or on which machine, because the knowledge sits in the workspace.
Memory holds facts about your project. Skills hold the steps to follow. Together, they onboard an agent in seconds.
When something changes, the next agent updates the entry, so the answer is always the latest one.
There is no wiki to keep alive and no onboarding doc to chase. The workspace is the onboarding doc.
Ask once, know always. Try workspace memory at Agent R Q dot com.
